paper_title: Compact Piecewise Linear Model Based Temperature Control of Multicore Systems Considering Leakage Power

extraction.paper_title: Compact Piecewise Linear Model Based Temperature Control of Multicore Systems Considering Leakage Power

scenario.figure_or_table: Table I and Fig. 5 (16-core system, PWL DTM temperature tracking experiment; configuration in Fig. 3)
scenario.description: Published scenario: compact piecewise linear (PWL) model-based predictive dynamic thermal management of a 16-core system (4x4 cores, 20x20 thermal grid, 25 grids per core, with package structure, chip structure, and NoC architectural diagram in Fig. 3) considering temperature-dependent leakage power. Compared against linear-model MPC (traditional DTM) and echo state network DTM for temperature tracking toward a 70 C target in rising (about 30 C to 70 C) and falling (about 110 C to 70 C) cases. Control step is 1 s, and ambient is 20 C. The packet does not publish block coordinates or sizes, per-core watts, or a power time series.
scenario.architecture: 16-core multi-core processor on a 4x4 core layout (core11 to core44) connected by a network-on-chip, with TIM and package structure shown in Fig. 3; thermal model of order 1612 reduced to a 32-order compact model; 7 nm FinFET leakage model
scenario.workload: Dynamic power traces generated by the Wattch power estimator running standard SPEC benchmarks, randomly assigned to different cores; golden leakage power from iteration-based leakage-aware thermal simulation with 0.01 s step
scenario.operating_point: Target temperature 70 C, ambient 20 C, control step 1 s, Nc=1/Np=1, Nc=3/Np=4, Nc=5/Np=7; PWL with 3 to 11 expansion points; reported tracking differences of 0.209 to 0.438 C for PWL; core22 transient shown in Fig. 5 with 7 expansion points

original_setup.solver: The plant is a 16-core chip and package RC thermal model of order 1612. It uses a 20x20 chip grid (25 thermal nodes per core) and is simulated with an iteration-based leakage-aware transient method at a 0.01 s step. The controller's internal model is a compact PWL model made of local linear models (32-order, from sampling-based MOR with samples at 0, 0.5 and 1 Hz). Temperature states are estimated with a Kalman filter. (pdf pages 3-7)
original_setup.optimizer: Unconstrained least-squares MPC that minimizes J=(Yg-Y)^T(Yg-Y) with a closed-form solution (Eq. 22). The PWL model uses 3 to 11 Taylor expansion points, with horizons Nc=1/Np=1, Nc=3/Np=4 and Nc=5/Np=7. (pdf pages 5-8)
original_setup.controller: Compact PWL model-based predictive dynamic thermal management (PWL DTM). It outputs a future dynamic power recommendation that is applied through frequency scaling and task migration. The control step is 1 s, the target is 70 C, ambient is 20 C, and the rising and falling cases are about 30 to 70 C and about 110 to 70 C. It is compared with linear-model MPC (traditional DTM) and echo-state-network DTM (200 neurons). (pdf pages 6-8)
original_setup.benchmark: Dynamic power traces generated by Wattch from standard SPEC benchmarks, randomly assigned to cores of the 16-core system (core11 to core44) in Fig. 3. The leakage model is a 3rd-order polynomial fitted to a 7 nm PTM-MG FinFET HSPICE simulation. Results are in Table I and Fig. 5. (pdf pages 3, 6-8)

thermal_observable.location: Plant core temperature versus the 70 C target. The 0.209 value is the PWL DTM with 11 expansion points, falling case, Nc=3, Np=4.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Average temperature tracking difference between actual plant temperature and target temperature over the first three control steps, as reported in Table I.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper's problem is a closed-loop transient DTM problem with 1 s control steps, MPC power recommendations, a Kalman filter and rising/falling trajectories. It is not a steady-state placement or thermal-map problem, so a steady 2D static thermal run cannot reproduce it.
The experiment is about temperature-dependent leakage feedback, using a polynomial 7 nm FinFET leakage model and PWL linearization. A fixed-power thermal run omits this nonlinearity.

The packaged multi-core plant has a TIM/package structure shown in Fig. 3 and a 1612-order thermal model. Package layers, materials, cooling and boundary details are not given as numbers in the text and cannot be mapped to a bare 2D Studio model.

The controller (PWL-model MPC with DVFS/task-migration-style power recommendations) and the ESN and linear-MPC baselines are not part of a plain Studio thermal solve. Their results cannot be compared numerically with Studio temperatures.

The workload is randomly assigned Wattch/SPEC dynamic power traces, with golden leakage computed iteratively. Neither the per-core powers nor the time series are published, so no same-scenario power rows exist.
The NoC power is ignored by the authors (less than 2 mW per router). This is a minor simplification in the original setup.

methods.note: The paper's method (PWL-model MPC DTM with sampling-based MOR, Kalman filter, 1 s closed-loop control, rising and falling cases) is supported by text on pages 3-8. But experiment.kind='custom_2d_steady' contradicts the extraction's own steady_2d_relevant=false and its essential physical_mismatches. The scenario is transient, closed-loop, leakage-nonlinear and package-resolved (1612-order RC model), so it cannot be called a 2D steady reproduction.

code.note: No code, repository or availability statement appears on pages 1-10. The packet has no assets. The only links are the PTM device-model page (ref [23], page 9) and the author-hosted paper PDF, and neither is evidence of controller, plant or thermal-solver code.

parameters.note: Several scalars are confirmed as printed: 70 C target, 20 C ambient, 1 s step, 0.01 s golden step, 20x20 grid, 25 grids per core, order 1612 reduced to 32, 60 W on core11 (MOR test only), 3 sampling points. The summary range 'tracking differences of 0.209 to 0.438 C for PWL' is contradicted by Table I, whose maximum PWL value is 0.448 (rise, 3 points, Nc=3/Np=4). The note that Table I 'prints 0.209 and 0.21 elsewhere' is unsupported: the table prints 0.209 and 0.210 for other columns. The leakage polynomial coefficients, MPC weight R, Kalman settings and Taylor point and switching-time values are not published.

config.note: No numeric chip or core dimensions, no core block coordinates, and no package layer thicknesses, materials, TIM, heat sink or convection boundary conditions are provided. Fig. 3 on page 6 is a schematic only. It was not visually verified as an image because the evidence is pdftotext output and no assets were supplied, and it carries no scale to digitize. No Studio package or material assumptions are supplied.

findings.reason: The kind is 'custom_2d_steady' with an empty floorplan and no power. This contradicts steady_2d_relevant=false and the essential mismatches (transient closed-loop MPC, nonlinear leakage feedback, 1612-order packaged model, no published block geometry or power). A 2D steady reproduction would omit decisive transient, leakage and package features and would use invented shelf geometry and constant power.
The stated range 'tracking differences of 0.209 to 0.438 C for PWL' is wrong. Table I shows PWL rise 3 points at Nc=3/Np=4 as 0.448, and also 0.439 for Nc=5. The maximum is 0.448, not 0.438.

assessment.summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped; simulation_allowed=false). The input gate failed because the custom_2d_steady experiment has no floorplan blocks and no power_w object (1–128 blocks plus power_w are required). The scientific gate also failed. There is no Studio temperature, no steady map, and no transient trace. The final verdict is therefore gated to no simulation and comparison_valid=false. Nothing here replicates the paper. The paper scenario (W2994830312, Table I and Fig. 5) is closed-loop transient predictive DTM of a 16-core 4x4 system. It uses a compact PWL model of order 32 reduced from a 1612-order plant, 7 nm leakage feedback, a Kalman filter, a 1 s control step, a 70 C target and 20 C ambient. A static custom 2D steady run cannot represent this problem. The reported observable is 0.209 degC. It is an average tracking difference between plant core temperature and the 70 C target, in the falling case with PWL at 11 expansion points and Nc=3/Np=4, averaged over the first three control steps. It is a controller tracking error, not a thermal-solver temperature, so no numerical comparison with Studio is made. No bundled EV6/GCC adaptation and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace generated placement was used, so there is no illustrative input.flp, no one-row input.ptrace, and no source commit or placement assumption to report. The packet had no pinned assets, and the linked PTM page and author PDF are not pinned thermal inputs. At most, qualitative sensitivity can be discussed: leakage-temperature feedback, package and boundary conditions, and workload power would all shift temperatures and the controller's tracking. Comparison is blocked by mismatches in location, aggregation, regime, and boundary assumptions, enumerated in the limitations.
limitations: Studio was not run, so there are no simulated temperatures and no transient trace; comparison_valid=false and no numerical comparison with the paper's 0.209 degC is permitted.
Regime mismatch: the paper is closed-loop transient DTM with MPC, a Kalman filter and rising/falling trajectories; the screened experiment kind is custom_2d_steady.

Observable mismatch: 0.209 degC is an average controller tracking difference versus the 70 C target over the first three control steps, aggregated across cores. It is not a peak or steady temperature at a defined location.
Physics mismatch: temperature-dependent leakage with the polynomial 7 nm FinFET model and PWL linearization cannot be reproduced by a fixed-power thermal solve.
Boundary mismatch: the package, TIM, heat sink and convection details of Fig. 3 are not given numerically. The 1612-order plant cannot be mapped to a bare 2D model; only a 20 C ambient is stated.
Geometry missing: no block coordinates, core sizes or chip dimensions in meters are published. Only the 4x4 layout, a 20x20 grid and 25 grids per core are stated, and Fig. 3 has no scale.

Power missing: there are no per-core watts and no Wattch/SPEC power time series. The 60 W core11 step is a model-order-reduction accuracy test and not a DTM workload row, and 'several watts per core' is qualitative.
The controller and the ESN and linear-MPC baselines are not part of a plain Studio thermal solve.

No pinned assets were supplied; the PTM and paper PDF links are not pinned or available as inputs. No bundled EV6/GCC adaptation and no Ascend910/ATPlace pinned sizes, source commit or generated-placement assumption were used.

Gate failures: custom experiment lacks blocks and power_w, evidence items 18 and 19 lack a valid page or asset locator, there is no cited observable or regime, and the adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved or pending. Results are not independently verified.
